'''Mojżesz Presburger''', or '''Prezburger''',<ref name="Autexier.Benzmuller.Siekmann.2009"/> ({{IPA|pl|ˈmɔjʐɛʂ prɛzˈburgɛr}}; 27 December 1904 – {{abbr|c.|circa}} 1943) was a Polish [[Jew]]ish [[mathematician]], [[logician]], and [[philosopher]]. He was a student of [[Alfred Tarski]], [[Jan Łukasiewicz]], [[Kazimierz Ajdukiewicz]], and [[Kazimierz Kuratowski]].<ref name="Autexier.Benzmuller.Siekmann.2009"/> He is known for, among other things, having invented [[Presburger arithmetic]] as a student in 1929 – a form of arithmetic in which one allows induction but removes multiplication, to obtain a [[Decidability (logic)|decidable theory]].<ref>{{cite book | first=Mojżesz |last=Presburger | contribution=Über der Vollständigkeit eines gewissen Systems der Arithmetik ganzer Zahlen, in welchen die Addition als einzige Operation hervortritt | title=Comptes Rendus Premier Congrès des Mathématicienes des Pays Slaves, Varsovie 1929 / Sprawozdanie z I Kongresu matematyków krajów słowiańskich, Warszawa 1929 |editor-first=F. |editor-last=Leja | location=Warsaw, Lwów and Krakow |publisher=Ksiażnica atlas | pages=92–101, 395 | year=1930 }}</ref><ref>{{cite report | first=Ryan |last=Stansifer | title=Presburger's Article on Integer Arithmetic: Remarks and Translation | type=Technical Report | location=Ithaca/NY | publisher=Dept. of Computer Science, Cornell University | volume=TR84-639 | url=http://cs.fit.edu/~ryan/papers/presburger.pdf | date=Sep 1984 | access-date=2014-10-10 | archive-date=2015-02-06 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150206092011/http://cs.fit.edu/~ryan/papers/presburger.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{ cite journal |  first1=Mojżesz |last1=Presburger |first2= Dale |last2=Jacquette | title=On the Completeness of a Certain System of Arithmetic of Whole Numbers in Which Addition Occurs as the Only Operation | journal=History and Philosophy of Logic | volume=12 | pages=225–33 | year=1991 | issue=2 | doi=10.1080/014453409108837187 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Wolfram|first=Stephen|title=A New Kind of Science|publisher=Wolfram Media, Inc.|year=2002|page=1152|isbn=1-57955-008-8}}</ref>

He was born in Warsaw on 27 December 1904 to Abram Chaim Prezburger and Joehwet Prezburger (née Aszenmil).<ref>Birth certificate at https://www.mimuw.edu.pl/~bojan/presburger</ref> On 28 May 1923 he got his [[matura]] from the {{ill|School of Commerce of the Merchants' Meeting of Warsaw|pl|Szkoła Handlowa Zgromadzenia Kupców m. Warszawy}}.<ref>Matura document at https://www.mimuw.edu.pl/~bojan/presburger</ref> On 7 October 1930 he was awarded [[Master of Science|master]] in mathematics from [[Warsaw University]].<ref name="Autexier.Benzmuller.Siekmann.2009"/><ref>Graduation diploma at https://www.mimuw.edu.pl/~bojan/presburger</ref> He died in [[the Holocaust]], probably 1943.<ref name=" Feferman">{{cite book|last1=Burdman Feferman|first1=Anita|author1-link= Anita Burdman Feferman |last2= Feferman|first2=Solomon|author2-link=Solomon Feferman|title=Alfred Tarski: Life and Logic|url=https://archive.org/details/alfredtarskilife0000fefe|url-access=registration|quote=Presburger holocaust.|year=2004|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|isbn=978-0-521-80240-6|page=[https://archive.org/details/alfredtarskilife0000fefe/page/74 74]}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | first=Jan |last=Zygmunt | title=Mojżesz Presburger: Life and Work | journal=History and Philosophy of Logic | volume=12 | pages=211–223 | year=1991 | issue=2 | doi=10.1080/014453409108837186}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | first=Jan |last=Woleński | title=Logic and Philosophy in the Lvov-Warsaw School | location=Dordrecht | publisher=Reidel | year=1988 | isbn=978-9027727497 | url-access=registration | url=https://archive.org/details/logicphilosophyi0000wole }}</ref><ref name="Autexier.Benzmuller.Siekmann.2009">{{cite report | first1=Claus-Peter |last1=Wirth |first2=Jörg |last2=Siekmann |first3= Christoph |last3=Benzmüller |first4= Serge |last4=Autexier | title=Lectures on Jacques Herbrand as a Logician | institution=DFKI | type=SEKI Report | number=SR-2009-01 | arxiv=0902.4682 | year=2009 }}; Here: p.48, footnote 128</ref>

In 2010, the [[European Association for Theoretical Computer Science]] began conferring the annual [[Presburger Award]] named after him to a young scientist (in exceptional cases to several young scientists) for outstanding contributions in theoretical computer science.  [[Mikołaj Bojańczyk]] was the first recipient.
